title: A Choir for the Spire Revisited
premise: Odile Oyelaran keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, and she has quietly kept one of her own thefts off the books for years: a memory that belongs to a dead god. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin receiving answers, the god's surviving kin come hunting their sibling's last fragment, and Odile discovers her own childhood memories are stitched from what she stole. To survive, she must decide whether to return the memory — erasing the self she built around it — or keep it and reignite the war that killed the gods' generation. In the end she gives it back, but negotiates a new covenant: the gods will answer only what mortals willingly surrender, making her guild's ledgers the treaty itself.
about_author: Silas Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era debt ledgers before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, inheritance, and the people history forgets to bill.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She audits the guild's memory-vaults by candlelight, showing how memories are weighed, priced, and pawned. A routine entry — a jar labeled only with her own handwriting — makes her hands shake. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Prayer Received
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A beggar's prayer at the Spire is answered for the first time in three centuries: his dead daughter's voice returns in the well water. The city celebrates; Odile recognizes the miracle's timbre as identical to the memory in her hidden jar. Beat: wonder curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Cut
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vane's POV. Vane learns of the answered prayer and orders every pre-Exile artifact audited, knowing exactly what sits unlisted in Odile's care. He offers her partnership in selling access to the returning gods. Beat: seductive corruption.

chapters.title: What the Jar Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Alone, she opens the jar a crack and experiences a stranger's death: a god dying and hiding its final memory inside a mortal bloodline — hers. Her 'childhood' flickers as forgery. Beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: The Kin Arrive
chapters.summary: New POV: Ashen, a god-remnant wearing a customs clerk's body. Ashen traces the resurrection's resonance to the guild and begins politely, terribly interviewing staff. Beat: civilized menace.

chapters.title: Debtors' Choir
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She seeks out guild clients who pawned memories of the old rites, assembling fragments of the war's true history. Their traded-away pasts leave them hollow, grateful, and strange. Beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane sells Ashen a map of the vaults — everything except the seventh floor. He intends to broker peace between gods and mortals with himself as toll-keeper. Beat: ambition dressed as statesmanship.

chapters.title: The Seventh Floor
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She moves the jar through the guild's blind spots with help from Tovi, a deaf apprentice who reads lips and lies fluently. First near-discovery by Ashen. Beat: heist tension and found-family warmth.

chapters.title: Ashen's Grief
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. We learn why the kin hunt: the hidden memory contains not just their sibling's death but their own shared guilt — they abandoned the dying god. Ashen wants it destroyed, not recovered. Beat: antagonist becomes tragic.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ashen corners her and asks what she remembers of her mother. Odile lies beautifully, then realizes Ashen already knows — this was a courtesy warning. Beat: terror braided with unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: The City That Prayed
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Miracles spread; the poor trade memories wholesale for answered prayers, and the guild's business booms obscenely. Odile watches survival priced by the pound. Beat: thematic crescendo of complicity.

chapters.title: Tovi's Question
chapters.summary: Tovi's POV. Tovi asks why Odile gets to keep a stolen life when clients lose theirs daily. Odile has no honest answer. Their friendship cracks. Beat: moral reckoning from an innocent.

chapters.title: Ledger Fire
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Rival factions within the guild, learning of the god-memory, torch the archives to erase debts. The vaults breach; loose memories flood the streets as fugues and weeping strangers. Beat: chaos, consequences.

chapters.title: What Escaped
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Amid the breach, the jar's contents partially leak: the dead god's voice speaks through a hundred strangers, calling Odile by a name she never chose. Beat: haunting revelation — she was made as a vessel.

chapters.title: Ashen's Offer
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. Ashen proposes destroying the memory together, sparing the war but erasing Odile's borrowed self entirely. Odile must weigh authenticity against existence. Beat: devastating choice framed as kindness.

chapters.title: The Name Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Digging into guild founding records, she finds the Vellum Guild was built by survivors of the war specifically to imprison the memory — and her bloodline was its lock. Beat: inheritance as sentence.

chapters.title: Vane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. With the archives burned, Vane claims sole knowledge of the memory's location and opens negotiations with all surviving god-kin, offering war or worship at his price. Beat: villain's triumph.

chapters.title: A Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile gathers everyone the guild ever wronged — debtors, Tovi, hollowed clients — proposing they answer the gods collectively, drowning Vane's monopoly in a chorus of willing surrender. Beat: hope forged from damage.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Spire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vane's hired blades and Ashen's kin converge on the spire where Odile will speak the covenant. Battle among falling memories; Tovi is gravely hurt shielding the ledger. Beat: climax begins, cost made real.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Covenant
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Before gods and mob alike, Odile returns the memory — surrendering her false childhood — and reads the new terms aloud: no prayer answered except from willing gift. The dead god's voice names her truly at last. Beat: sacrifice and self-authorship.

chapters.title: What the Gods Owe
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. The kin accept the covenant rather than resume extinction; Ashen, freed of guilt's secret, chooses to remain mortal-bodied and tend the well where it began. Beat: grief resolved into stewardship.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, the guild reopens under joint mortal-divine charter, its ledgers now recording gifts freely given. Odile, memoryless of her old self but writing a new one, takes on Tovi as partner. Final line echoes chapter one's audit — this time, nothing hidden. Beat: earned peace, identity chosen.
